title: Dwarf galaxy: small but perfectly formed
caption: The dwarf irregular galaxy UGC 9128, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: UGC 9128 · constellation Bootes · about 8 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows UGC 9128, a dwarf irregular galaxy. Hubble clearly resolves its individual stars, and many much more distant galaxies appear in the background.

Most galaxies are either elliptical or spiral, but some fall into a catch-all group called irregulars, with no well-defined shape. UGC 9128 is also a dwarf, probably containing only about one hundred million stars, a small fraction of what a large spiral like the Milky Way holds.

Dwarfs matter because big galaxies are thought to be built up through mergers of smaller ones, which makes dwarfs a kind of building block. Astronomers have asked whether dwarfs share the structure of big galaxies, with older stars in a rounded halo and younger stars in a flat disc. Observations of UGC 9128 suggest that it does.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.21 x 3.15 arcminutes) and distance (8 million light years), the frame spans roughly 7,500 × 7,300 light-years. Its light set out about 8 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the Wide Field Channel of Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. A yellow-orange filter is coloured blue and a near-infrared filter is coloured red.
understand.eye: The colours are shifted from natural hues, part of the data is near-infrared light, and the galaxy is too faint to see by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: UGC 9128 lies about 8 million light-years away in the constellation Boötes, the Herdsman. Though fairly close, it is so faint that nobody found it until the twentieth century.
alt: A galaxy of individually resolved stars with no well-defined shape, with many small distant galaxies in the background.
